title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6731 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

The FX option expiration price levels refer to the strike prices where option contracts are set to expire. These levels include both calls and puts. When you see "EUR/USD at 1.1600 for €4 billion" it means there is a total of €4 billion worth of options (calls + puts combined) that have a strike price of 1.1600 and are expiring at that specific time (the "New York Cut" at 10:00 AM ET). Traders watch these levels because they often act as a "magnet" for the price. For example, if there's nothing happening in the market and the price is close to the expiry level, let's say 30-50 pips away, what you will usually see is the price moving into the expiry level. This happens due to the hedging activity of the market makers (banks, dealers and so on). As the price gets closer to the strike price near expiration, these market makers must aggressively buy or sell the currency to hedge their risk. This hedging activity tends to suppress volatility and keep the price "pinned" close to the strike price until the expiration time passes. title: The stock market's wealth effect: why it matters even if you don't own stocks
body: Equity market movements can have a significant impact on the economy through the so-called "wealth effect", changes in financial conditions and the influence on corporate investment and hiring decisions. People can be affected by a stock market rally or selloff, even if they don't own stocks. Companies rely on financial markets to raise capital, finance expansions, make acquisitions and attract investment. When equity markets rise or collapse, the consequences can eventually reach workers, consumers and businesses across the economy. Households wealth The most straightforward transmission channel is the household wealth effect. When stock prices rise, households with equity exposure become wealthier, at least on paper. This includes people holding individual stocks, ETFs and mutual funds, as well as workers with retirement accounts and pension investments. As their portfolios appreciate, households may feel more financially secure and become more comfortable increasing consumption. They might purchase a new car, renovate their homes, travel more frequently or increase discretionary spending. This is the positive wealth effect as rising asset prices support consumer confidence and spending, providing an additional boost to economic growth. The reverse is also true. When stock prices fall sharply, households suffer a decline in financial wealth.

Feb Live Cattle futures rose $0.50 on Friday to settle at $227.70, bringing the weekly gain to $2.90 even as the S&P 500 fell 7% and the Nasdaq-100 dropped as much as 9%. Ahead of the afternoon Cattle on Feed report, average analyst estimates pegged on-feed supplies at 99.7%, marketings at 94.9% and placements at 97%. Firm wholesale boxed beef values also provided support, with choice cuts rising $1.77 to $355.29 and select cuts gaining $2.53 to $344.50. Thursday cattle slaughter reached 110,000 head, bringing the week-to-date total to 438,000 head, or 32,000 fewer than a year ago. Jan Feeder Cattle futures dipped $0.12 on the session to $335.42 while holding a $0.07 weekly gain, leaving Feeder Cattle CVOL steady at 17.66%. Meanwhile, Feb Lean Hog futures declined $1.07 to $56.97, ending the week down $4.40, or about 7%.

title: Corn futures hit weekly close low as Soybeans test resistance.
body: Grain markets traded mixed on Friday ahead of December options expiration and next week's first notice day, prompting continued volume roll from December into March contracts. Mar Corn futures slipped 3.75 cents to settle at 448'6, marking an 8-cent weekly loss and a new weekly closing low. Weekly corn export sales totaled 1.59 million metric tons, led by Mexico, though volumes fell 45% from the prior week. In contrast, Jan Soybean futures rose 13.25 cents to 1220'6, testing resistance at the 20-day moving average and trimming their weekly decline to 11 cents. Soybean export sales reached 1.5 million metric tons, up 30% week over week with China as the top buyer. Meanwhile, Mar Chicago Wheat futures declined 3 cents on the session to end the week at 592'0, down 14.75 cents or roughly 2.5% as U.S. dollar strength pressured prices despite an 89% weekly jump in export sales to 345,000 metric tons.

That move has taken the price from a high on November 10 at 0.69296 to the low today at 0.6609 or -320 pips. The 320-pip slide in AUDUSD started with a repricing of Fed rate expectations and picked up steam as Australia's jobs market weakened and the global equity selloff deepened. The Aussie's 2.30% decline this week, the largest of the seven majors you tracked against the USD, also reflected weakness against other currencies, including the yen and euro. Hot US inflation got the USD rally going. The November 10 CPI report showed prices rising 0.4% month over month vs. 0.3% expected. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point December hike should be considered. That pushed traders to price in a more aggressive Fed and helped lift the dollar index to its highest level since April 2025. investing.com Australia's jobs report took away rate support for the Aussie. The RBA had just raised its cash rate to 4.85% on November 3, but after the jobs report, swaps dropped bets on another hike and priced in easing for 2027.
